We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (para-aminophenyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the tolyl ring (para? Actually tolyl is attached to sulfonyl as N-sulfonyl). So we have N-sulfonyl aniline? Wait: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2: the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to tolyl ring (the N is attached to tolyl? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So tolyl ring has NSO2- attached (sulfonamide). The N is attached to tolyl, and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring (aryl sulfone). So it's a sulfonamide linking two aryl groups.

Thus retrosynthesis could break the sulfonamide bond (S-N) via sulfonyl chloride + aniline? Typically sulfonamide formed by reacting sulfonyl chloride with amine. So we could disconnect at S-N to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The aryl sulfonyl chloride could be derived from the second phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide substituent. So step1: sulfonyl chloride formation from that phenyl sulfonyl chloride (maybe from sulfonyl chloride reagent). The second phenyl ring also has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). That side chain could be formed via Heck coupling (C=C formation) or via condensation (Knoevenagel) then amidation. Simpler: we could disconnect the amide bond (C=O-N) to give an acid (trans-α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid could be formed via Wittig or Heck but maybe easier: start from trans-cinnamic acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH) then amidate with aniline to give trans-cinnamoyl aniline (the side chain). Then attach that phenyl ring to sulfonyl chloride via sulfonylation? Actually the phenyl ring bearing the side chain is the same as the sulfonyl chloride aromatic ring. So we need a phenyl sulfonyl chloride that already has the side chain attached. Could we start from 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)phenyl sulfonyl chloride? That could be made by sulfonyl chloride formation on a phenyl ring that already has the side chain. So we could start from 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride can be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid via thionyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Target (T)

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide N-S bond -> precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl with side chain). Reaction: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide.

Step 2: Disconnection of amide bond in side chain -> precursors: trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamoyl chloride) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the side chain is attached to the phenyl ring via amide: C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (aniline). So we can form amide by reacting trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) with 4-aminophenyl (aniline). But note the aniline is attached to the side chain as N attached to carbonyl, and also has an NH2 on the phenyl (the aniline). So the amide is between trans-cinnamic acid and 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl). So step2: trans-cinnamic acid + 4-aminophenyl (aniline) -> trans-cinnamoyl aniline (amide). Reaction: amide coupling (e.g., using EDC/HOBt). So we need trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and 4-aminophenyl (aniline) (commercial). Good.

Step3: The sulfonyl chloride precursor: 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonyl chloride can be made from 4-(trans-cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonic acid (or the corresponding sulfonyl chloride). Starting from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we need the sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring that also has the amide substituent. Could we start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and then amidate? But the amide is on the para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring at position 1, and the side chain at para position (maybe). So we could start from p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and then do a Suzuki coupling to attach the side chain? Actually side chain is a trans-cinnamoyl anilide attached via a phenyl ring (the same phenyl). So we need to attach the side chain onto the phenyl ring via a C-C bond (aryl-alkenyl). Could be via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with trans-cinnamyl? But maybe easier: start from 4-bromo-benzoic acid derivative? Might be complex.

Alternative route: disconnect the C=C bond (Heck) to give aryl bromide and trans-cinnamoyl amide? Actually the side chain is attached via a phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph. The C=C is between phenyl ring and carbonyl carbon? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)N-... The double bond is between phenyl ring (attached to sulfonyl) and carbonyl carbon? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-N. So the phenyl ring is attached to the alkene carbon (beta carbon). So the double bond is conjugated with phenyl. So we could form that via Wittig from aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and phosphonium ylide of acyl? Or via Heck coupling of aryl halide with acrylamide? Could be simpler: start from 4-(acrylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride (i.e., the phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride and an acrylamide substituent). Then perform a cross-metathesis with styrene? But maybe we can use a Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acrylamide to give the trans-alkene.

Thus step2 could be formation of the aryl acrylamide (C=O-NH-Ph) attached to phenyl ring via double bond. Actually the double bond is between phenyl and carbonyl carbon, not between phenyl and carbonyl? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)N: The SMILES fragment: /C=C/C(=O)N. So the phenyl ring attaches to the first carbon of the double bond (the beta carbon). So the double bond is between phenyl carbon (attached to sulfonyl phenyl) and the carbonyl carbon's alpha carbon? Actually the carbonyl carbon is after the double bond: C=C-C(=O)N. So the double bond is between phenyl carbon and carbonyl alpha carbon (CH). So the side chain is phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph. So we need to form that alkene via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph). So step2: aryl bromide (4-bromo-benzenesulfonyl chloride) + acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph) -> trans-aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph (Heck). Then step1: sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine -> sulfonamide.

Thus overall 2 steps? Actually we have three steps: Step1: sulfonamide formation (final). Step2: Heck coupling to form alkene. Step3: preparation of acrylamide (maybe from acryloyl chloride + aniline). But we can consider acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph) commercially available? Yes, acryloyl anilide (acrylamide with aniline) maybe not common. But we could use acryloyl chloride + aniline to make acryloyl anilide (acrylamide). That is step3.

Thus route:

Target T.

Step A (retro): disconnect sulfonamide -> precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and 4-(trans-cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride (intermediate I1).

Step B: disconnect alkene via Heck -> precursors: 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (I2) and N-phenylacrylamide (I3).

Step C: disconnect amide of acryloyl -> precursors: acryloyl chloride (I4) and aniline (I5).

All leaves: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, acryloyl chloride, aniline. All are commercially available and cheap.

We need to verify template IDs for each reaction. Use search to find templates for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also for Heck coupling (aryl bromide + acrylamide). Also for amide formation (acryloyl chloride + amine). Let's search.
